en: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'Abdullah ibn Zam'ah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, delivered a sermon in which he mentioned the she-camel and mentioned the one who hamstrung her, saying: "When the most wretched of them sprang forth, there sprang forth to hamstring her a man influential, fierce, and protected among his clan, like Abu Zam'ah." Then he mentioned women and admonished concerning them, then said: "Why does one of you flog his wife"—in the narration of Abu Bakr: "flogging a slave-girl"—and in the narration of Abu Kurayb: "flogging a slave, and yet he might lie with her at the end of his day?" Then he admonished them regarding laughing at the passing of wind, saying: "Why does one of you laugh at what he does himself?"

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'bad ibn Khalid, who said: I heard Harithah ibn Wahb al-Khuza'i say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Shall I not inform you of the people of Paradise? Every weak person who is deemed weak; if he were to adjure Allah by an oath, He would fulfill it. Shall I not inform you of the people of the Fire? Every harsh, cruel, arrogant person."
Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us with this chain of narration, the like of it, except that he said: "Shall I not direct you..."

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us: Ma'bad ibn Khalid narrated to me that he heard Harithah ibn Wahb say that he heard the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say: "Shall I not inform you of the people of Paradise?" They said: "Yes." He, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Every weak person who is deemed weak; if he were to adjure Allah by an oath, He would fulfill it." Then he said: "Shall I not inform you of the people of the Fire?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Every cruel, boastful, arrogant person."

Abu Kurayb and Ahmad ibn 'Umar al-Waki'i narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, tracing it back to the Prophet: "The distance between the two shoulders of a disbeliever in the Fire is the journey of three days for a swift rider." And al-Waki'i did not mention: "in the Fire."

Surayj ibn Yunus narrated to me: Humayd ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Harun ibn Sa'd, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "The molar tooth of a disbeliever or the canine tooth of a disbeliever is like Uhud, and the thickness of his skin is a three days' journey."

Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli and Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: 'Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated to me that his father narrated to him from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, Death will be brought until it is placed between Paradise and the Fire, then it will be slaughtered. Then a caller will call out: 'O people of Paradise, there is no death! And O people of the Fire, there is no death!' Thereupon the people of Paradise will increase in joy upon their joy, and the people of the Fire will increase in grief upon their grief."

Zuhayr ibn Harb, al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani, and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us—'Abd said: reported to me, while the other two said: Ya'qub—namely Ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd—narrated to us: My father narrated to us, from Salih: Nafi' narrated to us that 'Abdullah said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Allah will admit the people of Paradise into Paradise and admit the people of the Fire into the Fire. Then an announcer will stand between them and say: 'O people of Paradise, there is no death! And O people of the Fire, there is no death! Each is abiding eternally in that which they are in.'"

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "When the people of Paradise are admitted into Paradise and the people of the Fire into the Fire, it will be said: 'O people of Paradise!'" then he mentioned with the meaning of the hadith of Abu Mu'awiyah, except that he said: "That is His words, Mighty and Majestic," and did not say: "then the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, recited," nor did he mention: "and he pointed with his hand to the worldly life."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us—and they were close in wording—saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection as if it were a black-and-white ram"—Abu Kurayb added: "and it will be made to stand between Paradise and the Fire"—and they agreed on the rest of the hadith—"so it will be said: 'O people of Paradise, do you recognize this?' They will crane their necks and look and say: 'Yes, this is death.' He said: And it will be said: 'O people of the Fire, do you recognize this?' He said: They will crane their necks and look and say: 'Yes, this is death.' He said: Then an order will be given concerning it and it will be slaughtered. He said: Then it will be said: 'O people of Paradise, eternity and no death! And O people of the Fire, eternity and no death!'" He said: Then the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, recited: {"And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter is concluded while they are in heedlessness and they do not believe"}, and he pointed with his hand toward the worldly life.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: 'Affan narrated to us: Hammad—meaning Ibn Salamah—narrated to us: Thabit reported to us, saying: I heard Anas say from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said: "There will remain of Paradise whatever Allah wills to remain, then Allah the Exalted will bring into being for it a creation from whatever He wills."

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ar-Ruzzi narrated to us: 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' narrated to us regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: {"On the Day We will say to Hell, 'Are you filled?' and it will say, 'Are there any more?'"}: He reported to us from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, that he said: "Hell will continue to have people thrown into it, and it will say: 'Are there any more?' until the Lord of Might places His foot in it, whereupon parts of it will draw together and it will say: 'Enough, enough, by Your Might and Your Generosity!' And there will remain surplus space in Paradise until Allah creates a new creation for it and settles them in the surplus of Paradise."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: 'Abd as-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us: Aban ibn Yazid al-'Attar narrated to us: Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, with the meaning of the hadith of Shayban.

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Shayban narrated to us, from Qatadah: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us that the Prophet of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Hell will continue to say: 'Are there any more?' until the Lord of Might, Blessed and Exalted, places His foot in it, whereupon it will say: 'Enough, enough, by Your Might!' and parts of it will draw together."

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Paradise and the Fire disputed..." and he mentioned the like of the hadith of Abu Hurayrah up to his words: "and for each of you it is incumbent upon Me to fill it," and he did not mention what came after it of the addition.

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: 'Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him—and he mentioned hadiths, among which: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Paradise and the Fire debated with each other. The Fire said: 'I have been favored with the arrogant and the tyrants.' And Paradise said: 'What is the matter with me that none enters me except the weak of the people, the humble among them, and the unheeded?' Allah said to Paradise: 'You are but My mercy; through you I have mercy upon whomever I will of My servants.' And He said to the Fire: 'You are but My punishment; through you I punish whomever I will of My servants. And for each one of you is its fill.' As for the Fire, it will not be filled until Allah, Blessed and Exalted, places His foot, whereupon it will say: 'Enough, enough, enough!' It is then that it will be filled and parts of it will draw together, and Allah does not wrong anyone among His creation. As for Paradise, Allah will bring into being for it a creation."

'Abdullah ibn 'Awn al-Hilali narrated to us: Abu Sufyan—meaning Muhammad ibn Humayd—narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Paradise and the Fire disputed," and he recounted the hadith with the meaning of the hadith of Abu az-Zinad.

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: Shababah narrated to us: Warqa' narrated to me, from Abu az-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said: "The Fire and Paradise debated with each other. The Fire said: 'I have been favored with the arrogant and the tyrants.' And Paradise said: 'What is the matter with me that none enters me except the weak of the people, the humble among them, and the powerless?' So Allah said to Paradise: 'You are My mercy; through you I have mercy upon whomever I will of My servants.' And He said to the Fire: 'You are My punishment; through you I punish whomever I will of My servants, and for each one of you is its fill.' As for the Fire, it will not be filled until He places His foot upon it, whereupon it will say: 'Enough, enough!' It is then that it will be filled and parts of it will draw together."

Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu az-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "The Fire and Paradise argued. This one said: 'The tyrants and the arrogant enter me.' And this one said: 'The weak and the poor enter me.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to this one: 'You are My punishment; through you I punish whomever I will'—and perhaps he said: 'I afflict through you whomever I will'—'and He said to this one: You are My mercy; through you I have mercy upon whomever I will, and for each one of you is its fill.'"

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar both narrated it to us: Rawh narrated to us: Sa'id narrated to us with this chain of narration, and he used "his waist" in place of "his waist-wrapper level".

'Amr ibn Zurarah narrated to me: 'Abd al-Wahhab—meaning Ibn 'Ata'—reported to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, who said: I heard Abu Nadrah narrate from Samurah ibn Jundab that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Among them are those whom the Fire will seize up to their ankles, among them are those whom the Fire will seize up to their knees, among them are those whom the Fire will seize up to their waist-wrapper level, and among them are those whom the Fire will seize up to their collarbones."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Shayban ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman narrated to us: Qatadah said: I heard Abu Nadrah narrate from Samurah that he heard the Prophet of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say: "Indeed, among them are those whom the Fire will seize up to their ankles, among them are those whom it will seize up to their waist-wrapper level, and among them are those whom it will seize up to their neck."

Muhammad ibn 'Abbad and Ibn Abi 'Umar both narrated it to us: Marwan narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Kaysan, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah with this chain of narration, and he said: "This has fallen into its bottom, so you heard its thud."

Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to us: Khalaf ibn Khalifah narrated to us: Yazid ibn Kaysan narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, when he heard a thud, whereupon the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Do you know what this is?" We said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "This is a rock that was thrown into the Fire seventy autumns ago, and it has been falling through the Fire until now, when it has reached its bottom."

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: 'Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, similar to the hadith of Abu az-Zinad, except that he said: "each of them being equal to its heat."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Al-Mughirah—meaning Ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman al-Hizami—narrated to us, from Abu az-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "This fire of yours, which the son of Adam kindles, is one part of seventy parts of the heat of Hell." They said: "By Allah, it would surely have been sufficient, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: "It has been favored over it by sixty-nine parts, each of them being equal to its heat."

'Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us: My father narrated to us, from al-'Ala' ibn Khalid al-Kahili, from Shaqiq, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Hell will be brought on that Day with seventy thousand bridles, with each bridle seventy thousand angels dragging it."

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: 'Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar reported to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him—and he mentioned hadiths, among which: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created Adam in His image, his height being sixty cubits. When He created him, He said: 'Go and greet those individuals—a group of angels who were sitting—and listen to how they answer you, for it will be your greeting and the greeting of your offspring.' He said: So he went and said: 'As-Salamu 'alaykum (Peace be upon you).' They said: 'As-Salamu 'alayka wa Rahmatullah (Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah).' He said: So they added: 'and the mercy of Allah.' He said: So everyone who enters Paradise will be in the form of Adam and his height sixty cubits. Creation has continued to diminish after him until now."

Hajjaj ibn ash-Sha'ir narrated to us: Abu an-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim al-Laythi narrated to us: Ibrahim—meaning Ibn Sa'd—narrated to us: My father narrated to us, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said: "There will enter Paradise people whose hearts are like the hearts of birds."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Usamah, 'Abdullah ibn Numayr, and 'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar; (and a different chain) Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us: 'Ubaydullah narrated to us, from Khubayb ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman, from Hafs ibn 'Asim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Sayhan, Jayhan, the Euphrates, and the Nile are all among the rivers of Paradise."
